TITLE: Iran may escalate attacks on UAE amid rumors of renewed war - analysis
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-17 16:33 (updated 18:41)
AUTHOR: Seth J. Frantzman
SOURCE: Jerusalem Post

KEY FACTS:
- Drone struck electrical generator outside inner perimeter of Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in Al-Dhafra Region, UAE, on Sunday 17 May 2026
- Fire caused near (not inside) plant; no radiological release; no injuries
- Abu Dhabi Media Office confirmed essential systems operating normally
- Federal Authority for Nuclear Regulation: plant's essential systems unaffected, all units operating as normal
- IAEA expressed "grave concern" — situation being followed closely
- No claim of responsibility — Iran or Iranian proxies suspected

UAE SCALE OF ATTACKS:
- UAE Minister of State at Foreign Ministry Khalifa Shaheen Al Marar at BRICS meeting Friday: UAE has been subjected to "repeated and unjustified Iranian terrorist attacks" since 28 February 2026
- UAE has intercepted ~3,000 attacks involving ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones
- Targets: airports, ports, oil facilities, desalination plants, energy networks, residential areas
- "UAE reserves its full sovereign, legal, diplomatic, and military rights to respond"

REGIONAL CONTEXT:
- AP cited: "highlighted the risk of renewed war as the Iran ceasefire remains tenuous"
- UAE Al-Ain media (Sunday): Israeli army "continues its preparations to resume the war"
- Reported plan: Israeli strike to include "damage to national infrastructure, energy sites, and power plants, and Israeli aircraft will also attempt to target high-ranking Iranian officials"
- Iran parliament speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf (US-Iran negotiator) being tasked with China-Iran ties
- Telegraph reported US prodded Iran to seize an Iranian island (?)
- Reports indicate "some Gulf states have been more active in the war than previously reported"
- Iran "closely watching Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Kuwait"
- NYT/WSJ reports of Israel establishing 1-2 sites in Iraq amid tensions
